# Benchmark sheet

<!-- Generated by demo/build_benchmark_sheet.py from benchmarks/baselines/2026-09-29/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every number below comes from a committed file under `benchmarks/baselines/2026-09-29/` (decision DM-2). Nothing is extrapolated. **These were not measured in Fabric**: live Fabric timings go in [`LIVE_TIMINGS.md`](LIVE_TIMINGS.md) after the owner's dry run.

## What was measured

- Machine: 4 cores, Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, `Linux-6.18.44-fc-v37-x86_64-with-glibc2.39`, Python 3.11.15.
- Each timing is the median of 5 runs (profiling) or 3 runs (retail), in a fresh process per run, runs interleaved between tools.
- The profiling numbers time the benchmark port `benchmarks/profile_1to1/port.py`, the vectorised numpy + pyarrow profiler that `shape.profile` was ported from. They were **not** measured on `shape.profile` itself. In the profiling table, `port MT` is the port's default threading (4 cores) and `port 1T` is one thread.
- Equivalence comes first: the same port output matches the reference profiler field by field on every dataset before its timing counts.

## Profiling: Spindle profiler vs vectorised port

Source: `profile_bench.json` (machine: 4 cores, started 2026-09-29 22:22:57); equivalence: `profile_verify.txt` (every field bitwise-identical on the datasets listed below).

| Dataset | Spindle 3.0.1 s | port MT s | port 1T s | speedup MT | speedup 1T |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| D1, 200k rows x 6 columns, Parquet | 1.42 | 0.18 | 0.23 | 8.1x | 6.3x |
| D2, 1M rows x 20 columns, Parquet | 26.51 | 1.82 | 4.83 | 14.6x | 5.5x |
| D2, 1M rows x 20 columns, CSV | 31.12 | 1.82 | 4.99 | 17.1x | 6.2x |
| D3, 5M rows x 10 columns, Parquet | 47.91 | 5.35 | 13.73 | 9.0x | 3.5x |
| D4, 100k rows x 200 columns, Parquet | 28.31 | 4.23 | 13.34 | 6.7x | 2.1x |
| MT, 3 tables (20k / 800 / 200k rows) with foreign-key detection | 2.01 | 0.38 | 0.36 | 5.3x | 5.6x |

## Retail data generation: Spindle vs vectorised port

Source: `retail_bench.json` (machine: 4 cores, seed 42, median of 3 runs, generate plus write Parquet). Equivalence: `retail_verify_medium.txt` and `retail_verify_large.txt` (columns equivalent: medium 60/60, large 60/60). The port runs with a different seed from Spindle, so the outputs are statistically equivalent within the verifier's tolerances, not bit-identical.

| Scale | Rows | Spindle 3.0.1 s | port s | speedup | peak RSS MB (Spindle / port) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| medium | 1,965,400 | 5.29 | 1.26 | 4.2x | 540 / 424 |
| large | 19,625,400 | 102.64 | 14.89 | 6.9x | 3353 / 2087 |

Data generation is not part of the early-access product (profiling only); this table is the equivalence-verified retail port that produces the demo data.
